analysis:
Examined docs/threat-model.yaml BASE lines 473–1395 and the supplied bounded patch against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. These excerpts cover inference cancellation, fail-closed response encryption, weight integrity, CPU/GPU data lifetime, cache encryption/account scoping/purge, attestation and serving authorization, privileged fan control, and local add-on availability. Historical limitations are not PR regressions.
The visible TB-012 patch adds an operator lifecycle mailbox alongside the signed add-on socket and explicitly preserves the same-user coordination limitation (BASE lines 815–818). The change index also identifies updates concerning accept-time authentication, socket overrides, self-reported busy fields, fail-open hold persistence, model-load fencing and control-path starvation. No supplied executable change or complete HEAD definition establishes a concrete weakened control; no finding is supported in this batch.
Integration must examine the remaining HEAD TB-012 text (lines 817–862), T-059 changes (2349–2355) and added threat text (2365–2398), together with the corresponding provider changes, to reconcile mailbox authorization, socket/control-file bounds, persistence failure behavior and model admission during holds. Relevant canonical boundaries/assets are TB-012, TB-011, A-018 and T-059; ensure holds do not stall App Attest renewal/revocation or encrypted inference cancellation. The partial patch and BASE-only units cannot establish the changed implementation's behavior or the adequacy of the new threat coverage. Platform busy-field routing remains an external contract, not an observed missing control.
